newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank gov pleased with market ERM response.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank gov pleased with market ERM response.

text.p: Finnish central bank governor Sirkka Hamalainen said on Monday she was pleased with market reaction so far to Finland's decision to link the markka to the ERM and that the markka's level was fully market driven.

In an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV), Hamalainen said Monday's foreign exchange market was very calm, adding that the Bank of Finland has in the past intervened only to remove sharp movements.
"That's why we have been very pleased with the exchange rate level and stablility (today) because it is fully market driven," Hamalainen said.

Asked if the bank was pleased with the reaction, she said "Oh yes we are. We really expected that there will be no changes or no turbulences in the markka because I believe markets have expected this linkage...and also, I think the level or the central rate was very much expected."
She repeated the central bank had no narrower bands in mind for markka fluctuation than the ERM's official 15 percent fluctuation bands.
"We don't have any narrower band for monetary policy purposes or for intervention purposes. That is very important," she said.

"If we would like to use narrower bands, it certainly would increase speculative attacks because if we came very near to that limit, there certainly are increasing speculations. That is one reason," she said.
"The second reason is that we have had a very stable currency (for two years), and we would like to see it continue that way. And we believe that it should."
Finland's economic fundamentals advocate stability, she added.

"We don't have any level where we are coming to intervene. We don't do anything like that. We really want to see that kind of development on the basis of stable fiscal policy income development and very stable monetary policy.
"Then if there are some speculative attacks we will have to make our decisions when we see what kind of developments we have," she added.
